2. Relevant facts for disposal of the Rule are that the opposite party as plaintiff filed a Title Suit No. 25 of 2014 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Bhedorganj, Shariatpur for cancellation of a Heba-bil-ewaz deed No. 495 dated 11-2-2010. The suit property appertaining to Plot Nos. 240, 241 and 242 under SA Khatian No. 102 belonged to Pochu Mal. He died leaving behind four sons namely Hanifa Mal, Sekandar Mal, Azizul Mal and Mojibul Mal and three daughters namely Halima Begum, Rahila Begum and Samsun Nahar and, as such, each son got 106 decimals of land and each daughter got 53 decimals of land by way of inheritance. Hanif Mal transferred 95 decimals of land to Sekandar Mal vide registered kabala deed No. 441 dated 15-6-1988. In this way Sekandar Mal became owner of (106 + 95) = 201 decimals of land by way of purchase and inheritance. Sekander Mal died leaving five sons namely Md Alamgir Mal, Md Osman Mal, Md Jahangir Mal, Md Moazzem Mal and Md Munsur Mal and five daughters namely Mosammat Khodeza Begum, Mosammat Majeda Begum, Mosammat Sajeda Begum, Mosammat Hajera Begum and Mosammat Mahmuda begum and wife Mosammat Belataun Nessa. The plaintiffs and heirs of Sekandar Mal have been possessing and cultivating the disputed land, but the defendant threatened on 22-4-2011 at 10-00 am to dispossess the plaintiff disclosing that their predecessor Md Sekander Mal transferred the suit property in favour of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 through registered kabala and thereafter they came to know about the alleged deed No. 495 dated 11-2-2010 registered in the Bhedorganj Sub-register Office but the Sekander Mal died on 24-1-2010. The alleged deed is a forged, illegal, ineffective, baseless and voidable deed created by false personation. The plaintiff filed the suit for declaration that the alleged Heba-bil-ewaz deed is a void and ineffective deed. Hence, the suit of the plaintiffs. 

 3. On the other hand the defendant No. 1 Sana Ullah Kha contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the allegations made in the plaint stating, inter alia, that Sekander Mal became owner of 2.50 acres of land in the disputed khatian by way of inheritance and purchase and he sold out the disputed land on 11-1-2010 on receiving value of Taka 1,16,000 and delivered possession to the defendant No. 1 but the deed writer wrote a Heba-bil-ewaz deed beyond the knowledge of the defendant although he purchased the land from Sekander Mal. The plaintiffs have no right, title, interest and possession over the suit land. They have filed a test suit which is liable to be dismissed.
